L00001: # Diagnostic Evaluation Benchmark towards Text-to-SQL Robustness
L00002: 
L00003: ## Description
L00004: This repo contains a diagnostic evaluation benchmark toward the robustness of text-to-SQL models, which contains 17 perturbation test sets to measure the robustness of models from different angles. It is released along with our ICLR 2023 paper: [Dr.Spider: A Diagnostic Evaluation Benchmark towards Text-to-SQL Robustness](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2301.08881.pdf).
L00005: The details can be found in our [paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2301.08881.pdf). 
L00006: 
L00007: The dataset is created using the dev set in the [Spider](https://yale-lily.github.io/spider) dataset and our changes to the Spider dataset are to supplement the work done by [Spider](https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.08887).
L00008: 
L00009: ## Preprocessing
L00010: 
L00011: First, unzip the data using the following command.
L00012: ```bash
L00013: mkdir data
L00014: tar -xvf data.tar.gz -C data
L00015: ```
L00016: 
L00017: Run ``data_preprocess.py`` to copy pre-perturbed databases and tables from the original spider devlopment set.
L00018: 
L00019: ```
L00020: python data_preprocess.py
L00021: ```
L00022: 
L00023: ## To Use
L00024: 
L00025: Each folder contains a perturbation test set. There are 3 DB perturbation test sets (starting with DB_), 9 NLQ perturbation test sets (starting with NLQ_), and 5 SQL perturbation test sets (starting with SQL_). Each test contains parallel pre-perturbation and post-perturbation test data. 
L00026: 
L00027: * `DB_*`: data with DB perturbation, which contain two database folders, two table files, and two question files, corresponding to pre-perturbation and post-perturbation data.
L00028: * `NLQ_*`: data with NLQ perturbation, which contain a single database folder, table file, and two question files (one for pre-perturbation and the other for post-perturbation).
L00029: * `SQL_*`: data with SQL perturbation, which contain a single database folder, table file, and two question files (one for pre-perturbation and the other for post-perturbation).
L00030: 
L00031: First, run the model on Spider-dev set to get the predicted SQL queries and put it in ``predictions/Spider-dev/[model_name]/pred.sql``.
L00032: Then, run the model on each post-perturbation set to get the predicted SQL queries in ``predictions/[perturbation_namq]/[model_name]/pred.sql``.
L00033: 
L00034: ## To Evaluate a Model
L00035: 
L00036: Run ``copy_pre_perturbation_predictions.py`` to generate copy the SQL prediction in Spider-dev to all pre-perturbation sets.
L00037: Evalaute the model on each pre-perturbation and post-perturbation set using the [test-suite evaluation](https://github.com/taoyds/test-suite-sql-eval).
L00038: 
L00039: ```
L00040: python copy_pre_perturbation_predictions.py --model [model_name]
L00041: ```
L00042: 
L00043: ## Leaderboard
L00044: 
L00045: ### Pre-perturbation and post-perturbation accuracy in terms of execution (EX)
L00046: The EX accuracy of models on pre-perturbation and post-perturbation data. We report the marco average results of the perturbation test sets in DB, NLQ, SQL sets. x-y represents the accuracy on pre-perturbation data and post-perturbation data.
L00047:

L00004: import os
L00005: import json
L00006: import argparse
L00007: 
L00008: if __name__ == "__main__":
L00009:     parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
L00010:     parser.add_argument('--model', type=str)
L00011:     args = parser.parse_args()
L00012:     model = args.model
L00013: 
L00014:     perturbation_categories={}
L00015:     perturbation_categories["DB"]=["schema_synonym","schema_abbreviation","DBcontent_equivalence"]
L00016:     perturbation_categories["NLQ"]=["keyword_synonym","keyword_carrier","column_synonym","column_carrier","column_attribute", "column_value", "value_synonym", "multitype", "others"]
L00017:     perturbation_categories["SQL"]=["comparison","sort_order","NonDB_number","DB_text","DB_number"]
L00018: 
L00019:     pred_path = f"predictions/Spider-dev/{args.model}/pred.sql"
L00020:     qid_to_pred = []
L00021:     with open(pred_path, "r") as f:
L00022:         for i, line in enumerate(f.readlines()):
L00023:             qid_to_pred.append(line.strip())
L00024: 
L00025:     for category in perturbation_categories:
L00026:         for subcategory in perturbation_categories[category]:
L00027:             with open(f"data/{category + '_' + subcategory}/questions_pre_perturbation.json", "r") as f:
L00028:                 pre_questions = json.load(f)
L00029:             if not os.path.exists(f"predictions/{category + '_' + subcategory}/{model}"):
L00030:                 os.makedirs(f"predictions/{category + '_' + subcategory}/{model}")
L00031:             with open(f"predictions/{category + '_' + subcategory}/{model}/pred_pre_perturbation.sql", "w") as f:
L00032:                 for q in pre_questions:
L00033:                     f.write(qid_to_pred[q["q_id_spider_dev"]] + "\n")
